<thought>Based on the ESI‑MS spectrum, the most intense ion is at m/z 233.963, which corresponds to a protonated molecule [M+H]⁺. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 232.956 Da. The isotopic pattern (M+2 peak ≈ 24 % of the base) is characteristic of a single chlorine atom (Cl‑35/Cl‑37). Removing the mass of Cl‑35 (34.969 Da) leaves ≈ 197.987 Da for the remaining atoms, which is best satisfied by the composition C₉H₁₀O₅. Adding the chlorine atom yields the molecular formula C₉H₁₀O₅Cl, which matches the observed exact mass within the experimental tolerance. 

Thus the molecular formula of the compound is: C9H10O5Cl.
